findings.message: The migration also switches the primary keys of all three tables from AutoField to BigAutoField. The story didn't ask for this, and on a large RateLimitEntry table it may rewrite and lock the table during `migrate`, which would block rate-limited requests. Lines 286-306 add `migrations.AlterField(... name="id", field=models.BigAutoField(...))` for ratelimitconfig, ratelimitcounter and ratelimitentry. 0001_initial.py creates those ids as `models.AutoField`. The change only needed the `AddField` for `data`. The ALTER is there because the migration was generated by makemigrations (header: 'Generated by Django 5.2.1') against apps.py `default_auto_field = "django.db.models.BigAutoField"`, which is unrelated to the bug.

The index renames run only when the installed Django has `RenameIndex`. Installs on Django 3.2 or 4.0, which the project still supports, end up with a different migration state and different database index names. On those versions the model's indexes no longer match migration state, so `makemigrations` would generate a new migration inside the installed package, and any later migration that relies on the new names will break. Line 232 has `RenameIndex = getattr(migrations, "RenameIndex", None)`, and line 243 has `if RenameIndex is not None: rename_operations.extend([...])`. pyproject.toml lists 'Framework :: Django :: 3.2' and '4.0' and requires `Django>=3.2`. The model Meta indexes in models.py are unnamed, so Django derives the new names, which differ from the names in 0001_initial (for example `django_smar_key_24c4a0_idx`).

The diff adds no test that database token buckets keep their state across requests. That is the behaviour the change exists to fix, yet the committed checklist marks 'Add or update automated tests' as done. Because the database errors are caught, a regression here would silently let every request through. diff.patch touches no file under tests/. tests/backends/test_database_backend.py has no `token_bucket_check` test, and tests/algorithms/test_token_bucket.py never refers to DatabaseBackend. CHECKLIST_database_backend_fix.md line 15 says `- [x] Add or update automated tests (unit/integration) that expose the bug and verify the fix.` The `except Exception` handler in `token_bucket_check` (lines 205-219) returns `True` (allowed) on any error, including a missing `data` column.

`get()` now runs stored values back through JSON parsing, so the type can change between `set()` and `get()`. For example, `set(k, "123")` reads back as int 123 and `set(k, "true")` reads back as bool True. `set()` stores `serialize_data(value)`, which returns `str(data)` for str, int and float. `get()` returns `deserialize_data(counter.data)`, and with no expected_type that is `json.loads(data)`. Any string that is valid JSON therefore comes back as a different type.

The migration has no tested rollback that keeps data. Reversing it drops the new `data` column and every serialized token-bucket state and `set()` value with it. Reversing BigAutoField to AutoField may fail once ids pass 2^31. The diff has no rollback rehearsal and no declared breaking-change path. The operations are a plain `AddField` (its reverse is RemoveField, so the column contents are lost) and `AlterField` to BigAutoField (its reverse narrows to int). There is no `RunPython` or state-preserving reverse, and the diff adds no test of the migration in either direction. The risk.json review focus asks: 'does the down path restore data, not just schema; is the rollback rehearsed?'

The change commits a working checklist to the repository root. It is unrelated to the story and contains a developer's absolute local paths. Its ticked boxes claim verification work that the diff doesn't show. This is a new file. It contains `/Users/<author>/Documents/GitHub/django-ratelimit-base/django-test-project` and `/Users/<author>/Documents/GitHub/django-test-project`, and every item is marked `[x]`, including running `make ci-check` and re-running the scenario.

`token_bucket_check` and `token_bucket_info` contain the same block for parsing stored bucket state, so a fix to one can easily miss the other. Lines 117-126 and 242-249 repeat the same sequence: `deserialize_data(counter.data, dict) if counter.data else {}`, the isinstance-dict guard, `float(bucket_data.get("tokens", counter.count))` and `float(bucket_data.get("last_refill", counter.updated_at.timestamp()))`. The two copies are not in a shared helper.

The new doc lines say `showmigrations` verifies that the `data` column exists. It only lists which migrations are recorded as applied and never inspects columns. backends.md also says 'Starting with the next release' instead of giving a version. installation.md adds `# Optional: verify that the RateLimitCounter table now includes the `data` column` followed by `python manage.py showmigrations django_smart_ratelimit`, and the same pairing appears again at line 265. docs/backends.md adds '> **Note:** Starting with the next release, `RateLimitCounter` includes a `data` column'. docs/design.md picks up a stray blank line at line 158.
